g.title: Sheet.1013
g.desc: Feature

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.46
g.desc: Scalability
g.text: Scalability

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.47
g.desc: Scaling is nearly instant and on-demand. You can add or remov...
g.text: You can scale up or down instantly. Adding or removing resources happens on demand, so I can match my business needs without waiting for new hardware.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.48
g.desc: Scaling requires buying and installing new hardware, which ca...
g.text: If you need to scale, you have to buy and install new hardware, which can take weeks or months. Growth is limited by physical space, power, and budget.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.42
g.desc: Cost
g.text: Cost

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.43
g.desc: Uses a subscription or pay-as-you-go model with minimal upfro...
g.text: You pay-as-you-go with no upfront costs. The expenses are operational, and while they can grow with usage, they’re more predictable and flexible.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.44
g.desc: You need to make a big upfront investment (CapEx) in servers,...
g.text: You need to make a big upfront investment (CapEx) in servers and networking gear. Then you have ongoing costs for electricity, cooling, and IT staff.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.51
g.desc: Security
g.text: Security

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.52
g.desc: Security is shared between provider and customer. The provide...
g.text: Security is a shared job: the provider protects the infrastructure, while you secure your applications and data.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.53
g.desc: Security is fully controlled by the organization, with custom...
g.text: You are fully in charge of the security. This gives you full control but also means you need skilled staff and constant updates to stay secure.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.55
g.desc: Compliance
g.text: Compliance

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.56
g.desc: Many providers are certified for global compliance standards,...
g.text: The provider is often certified for global compliance standards, which helps. Still, it’s on you to make sure their services actually fit your regional rules.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.57
g.desc: The organization is solely responsible for meeting regulatory...
g.text: You are the one responsible for meeting regulatory requirements and proving compliance. All audits and documentation have to be handled by your team.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.59
g.desc: Focus
g.text: Focus

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.60
g.desc: Cloud shifts the heavy lifting to the provider, freeing staff...
g.text: By using cloud, you let the provider handle most of the infrastructure. That frees you to focus more on strategy and business priorities.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.61
g.desc: IT teams spend significant time managing servers, patching sy...
g.text: Your IT team spend a lot of time managing servers, patching systems, and fixing outages. This can distract you from focusing on innovation and business.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.9
g.desc: Ownership
g.text: Ownership

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle.10
g.desc: The infrastructure and software are owned and managed by the ...
g.text: You don’t own the infrastructure — the cloud provider does. You only rent the resources, which means you have less control over the underlying systems.

g.title: Round Corner Rectangle
g.desc: You own the infrastructure - you have problems. You must hand...
g.text: You own the infrastructure - you have problems. You must handle hardware failures, updates, and security patches.
